claims.text: A blend of refractory high-entropy-alloy precursor powders and Cu powders is prone to phase segregation because of a large positive heat of mixing between refractory elements and Cu.
Rapid powder sintering, such as spark plasma sintering, can kinetically freeze the microstructure of RHEA–Cu composites.
Kinetic freezing by rapid sintering reduces phase separation induced by positive mixing enthalpy.
Rapid sintering can produce a stable, large-scale RHEA–Cu composite structure.
A machine-learning model can optimize the heating rate, dwell time, and cooling rate by screening non-equilibrium reaction kinetics.
High heating rates, short dwell times, and fast cooling rates limit diffusion during sintering.
The proposed high-temperature sintering conditions are suitable for large-scale reaction synthesis.
Rapid sintering produces a refined RHEA–Cu microstructure with reduced grain size.
Rapid sintering may form metastable interfacial phases in situ.
Metastable interfacial phases kinetically lock the Cu distribution within the refractory matrix.
Rapid sintering minimizes the time available for elemental diffusion.
Limiting elemental diffusion kinetically arrests phase separation between Cu and refractory elements.
Positive mixing enthalpy between Cu and refractory elements normally drives phase separation.
The proposed process will yield a stable composite microstructure containing well-dispersed Cu and refractory phases.
The rapidly sintered composite will have better high-temperature mechanical performance than conventionally processed structures.
The rapidly sintered composite will have better irradiation performance than conventionally processed structures.
Conventional slower sintering or casting of RHEA–Cu composites typically produces phase segregation and unstable microstructures.
The beneficial kinetic-arrest effect exists only within a narrow processing window.
Changes in sintering parameters, precursor purity, or composition may negate kinetic arrest and permit phase separation.
The exact processing window and long-term stability under reactor conditions remain undetermined.
